title: Processing 3D FIB-SEM Data via AIVE
author: Benjamin Padman
materials: Rename the each of the "materials" as follows: " 1Void " - To represent empty extracellular regions of the sample " 2Sol " - To represent granular protein content of the cytoplasm and nucleus " 3Matter " - To represent electron-dense homogenous materials that do not belong to a membrane (i.e. mitochondrial matrix) " 4Memb " - To represent cellular membranes. Alternatively, you can name the classes however you desire, provided that one of those classes is used to identify a class of structure that generates electron signal (i.e. membranes). This is required for AIVE.

steps.title: Pre-process 3D FIB-SEM Slices
steps.instruction: Prepare the dataset by selecting a subset of 3D FIB-SEM slices and registering them.

substeps.instruction: Deposit a subset of 3D FIB-SEM slices into a new directory.
In ImageJ/FIJI, run 'Plugins → Registration → Register Virtual Stack Slices'.
Set registration model and transformations to 'Translation only' and apply to the dataset folder.
Save the resulting TIFF stack.
Verify the pixel scale via 'Image → Properties'.
Crop the dataset to the smallest viable stack to remove empty regions caused by image drift.

steps.title: Perform CLAHE Processing
steps.instruction: Apply Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE) to the TIFF stack.

substeps.instruction: Place the original TIFF stack (with correct pixel scale) in a new directory.
Drag and drop the 'CLAHE-Batch-3DCLAHE-AnisotropicXYZ.ijm' script into FIJI and run it.
Select the directory containing the TIFF stack(s).
Do not interact with the computer until the process is complete to avoid switching the plugin window.

steps.title: Generate 3D Features
steps.instruction: Extract 3D features from the original TIFF stack using the 3DFeatSplitter script.

substeps.instruction: Drag and drop 'ML-Features-PART1-3DFeatSplitter-Sigma8.bsh' into FIJI and run it.

In the dialog box, configure the following 5 parameters: Input Stack (original TIFF stack), Output directory (HDD/SSD), Temporary directory (preferably SSD), Additional target slices per loop, and Starting Slice.
Optimize 'Additional target slices per loop' by starting low (2-3) and increasing if RAM allows, or decreasing if the system crashes.
Allow the process to run until completion.
Delete all files in the Temporary directory.

steps.title: Generate 2D Features
steps.instruction: Extract 2D features from the original TIFF stack using the 2DFeatSplitter script.

substeps.instruction: Drag and drop 'ML-Features-PART2-2DFeatSplitter.bsh' into FIJI and run it (expert users may adjust commented-out features at the end of the script).
In the dialog box, configure 3 parameters: Input Stack (original TIFF stack), Output directory (HDD/SSD), and Temporary directory (preferably SSD).
Allow the process to run until completion.
Delete all files in the Temporary directory.

steps.title: Combine 2D and 3D Features
steps.instruction: Merge the generated 2D and 3D feature sets into a final feature stack directory.

substeps.instruction: Drag and drop 'ML-Features-PART3-Combine3Dand2DFeatures.bsh' into FIJI and run it.
In the dialog box, select Folder 1 (3D Features), Folder 2 (2D Features), and the Output directory.
Once complete, the output directory (Feature Stack Directory) will contain individual TIFF stacks for each slice. You may now delete the original 2D and 3D features.

steps.title: Create Training Labels in MIB
steps.instruction: Annotate representative slices in the Microscopy Image Browser (MIB) to train the ML model.

substeps.instruction: Load the original TIFF stack into MIB.
Create a labeling model with at least 4 'materials' (classes), ensuring one represents electron-signal structures (membranes).
Randomly choose a slice containing representative examples of all materials and note the slice number.

Using the brush tool, annotate at least 2000 pixels for each of the following: 1Void (extracellular regions), 2Sol (cytosol/protein content), 3Matter (electron-dense homogenous materials), and 4Memb (cellular membranes).
Repeat this for at least 8 random slices, ensuring adequate coverage of the stack.
Save labels as TIFF slices: 'Model → Save Model As...' → 'Tiff Format (.tif)' → 'Sequence of 2D files' into a Training Label Directory.

steps.title: Extract Training Data
steps.instruction: Convert annotations and features into ARFF files for WEKA.

substeps.instruction: Drag and drop 'ML-CorePartA-ExtractTrainingDataFromFeatures.bsh' into FIJI and run it.

Configure 5 parameters: Feature Stack Directory, Binary Labels Directory (Training Label Directory), Output directory, File number to train (must be one of the annotated slices), and Num. of samples per class (must not exceed the number of pixels annotated for any class on that slice).
Repeat this process for each of the 8 annotated slices to generate 8 unique ARFF files in the Training Data Directory.

steps.title: Train Machine Learning Model in WEKA
steps.instruction: Pool training data and train a Random Forest classifier.

substeps.instruction: Open WEKA, click 'Simple CLI', and combine the ARFF files into a single pooled file using the command: java weka.core.Instances append "[PathToFile1.arff]" "[PathToFile2.arff]" > "[PathToCombined.arff]"
Open the pooled ARFF file in the WEKA 'Explorer' window.
Navigate to the 'Classify' tab and select 'Random Forest' (weka > classifiers > trees > RandomForest).
Set recommended parameters: bagSizePercent = 10, numFeatures = square root of available features, numIterations = 200, and seed = 1337.
Press 'Start' to train the model.
Right-click the result in the 'Results List' and save the trained model.

steps.title: Apply Classifier and Post-process
steps.instruction: Apply the trained WEKA model to the feature stacks and convert results.

substeps.instruction: Drag and drop 'ML-CorePartB-ApplyClassifierToFeatures.bsh' into FIJI and run it.
Configure 4 parameters: Features Directory (Feature Stack Directory), WEKA Model, Output Directory, and Starting Slice.
Once complete, run 'ML-postCorePartB-SlicesToStacks.ijm' in FIJI.
Select the output directory from the previous step and a new directory for converted outputs to generate raw probabilistic prediction stacks for each class (including 'Raw Membrane Predictions').

steps.title: Generate Organelle Class Stack
steps.instruction: Create a final label image TIFF stack where each voxel represents an organelle class.

substeps.instruction: Open MIB and load the original TIFF stack.
Create a new labeling model and add a 'material' for each organelle category.
Label each organelle of interest, ensuring the entire organelle is annotated and assigned to the correct material.
Save the labels as a '3D Tiff' via 'Model → Save Model As...' into an Organelle Class Stack.

steps.title: Prepare AIVE Directory Structure
steps.instruction: Organize all required inputs into a specific folder hierarchy.

substeps.instruction: Create a 'Main Directory' with five sub-directories: '0 Originals', '1 Masks', '2 Processed Masks', '3 Membrane Merge', and '4 FIB Merge'.
Copy the following into '0 Originals': CLAHE processed stack, Raw Membrane Predictions, and Organelle Class Stack.
Ensure the correct pixel scale is set for all images.

steps.title: Execute AIVE Processing Pipeline
steps.instruction: Run the sequence of AIVE macros to generate final results.

substeps.instruction: Run 'AIVE-Macro1-ConvertLabelImageToBinaryStacks.ijm': Select 'Organelle Class Stack' and '1 Masks' directory to create binary TIFF stacks per class.
Run 'AIVE-Macro2-GaussianFilterTheClassBinaries.ijm': Select '1 Masks' and '2 Processed Masks' directories to blur mask boundaries.
Run 'AIVE-Macro3-MergeMLoutputsWithClasses.ijm': Select 'Raw Membrane Predictions', '2 Processed Masks', and '3 Membrane Merge' directories.
Run 'AIVE-Macro4-MedianFilterTheCLAHEstacks.ijm': Create a 'CLAHE Median' sub-directory in '0 Originals', transfer CLAHE processed stacks there, and run the script to apply a 10nm radius median blur.
Run 'AIVE-Macro5-MergeTheMaskedMLoutputsWithCLAHE.ijm': Select the 3D Median filtered CLAHE processed stack, '3 Membrane Merge' directory, and '4 FIB Merge' directory.
